newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Still bullish on IBM, Kmart cools.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Still bullish on IBM, Kmart cools.

text.p: Investors were busy snapping up call options on International Business Machines Corp as the stock continued its amazing run Wednesday, traders said.
"We're doing a lot of IBM," said Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN Securities, citing the December 155s as being particularly busy.
The IBM December 155 call traded around 3,850 contracts by early afternoon, second in volume only to the 4,285 of the December 160 calls that traded.
Traders said despite the stock's strong rally over the last month or so, investors were not growing overly concerned.
Shares of the computer giant were up 1-1/4 at 155-3/8 Wednesday afternoon after climbing in early trade to 159, a nine-year high.
Turnover in the stock was heavy, with consolidated volume topping six million shares.

In the five trading sessions through Tuesday, the stock has rallied from about 133, helped by some positive brokerage house comments, including increased share price targets from Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley.
Despite the rally, investors were not aggressively buying puts for downside protection, traders said.
"You keep thinking this thing is going to pull back -- it's been straight up since about 137," Nothnagel said. "It's just been going like a rocket."
On the put side, nearly 3,500 of the IBM December 140 puts changed hands, as did 2,100 of the December 125 and 150 puts and nearly 2,100 of the January 135 puts.
Traders said both put and call buying was fairly heavy in the January and April series also.
In other trading, Kmart Corp options remained busy but traders said activity had slowed from the hectic, rumor-induced pace seen Tuesday.
Kmart shares and options were jolted Tuesday by talk that buyout firm Kohlberg Kravis & Roberts was interested in the retailer. Both Kmart and KKR declined comment.
"There was some interest on the opening, but things have calmed down significantly," said a trader in the Kmart trading crowd at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
"It's not nearly as busy as it was yesterday," he said.
He said volatilities declined a bit but investors were still focusing on out-of-the-money calls "because people are still gambling a little bit that it's going to go higher."
Kmart shares were off 3/8 at 10-7/8 in afternoon trade.
Kmart early Wednesday reported third quarter earnings that beat analysts' estimates.
Among the options, the December 10 call traded about 2,325 contracts, the January 12-1/2 call traded 2,260 and the January 10 call traded nearly 1,400.
The December 12-1/2 calls, January 15 calls and March 12-1/2 calls also were busy. The most active put was the December 10, with about 745 contracts traded.
The trader said better than expected third quarter earnings from retailer Dayton Hudson may have gotten the Kmart ball rolling Tuesday.--G.Crawford, (312) 408-8750
